newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani cotton closes steady, seen stable.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani cotton closes steady, seen stable.

text.p: Pakistani cotton rates closed steady on Saturday amid low buying by spinners and exporters, brokers at the Karachi Cotton Association (KCA) said.
In the kerb market, the NIAB-78 variety was quoted 2,050/2,175 rupees per maund (37.32 kg), the K-68 for 2,400/2,425 and the MNH-93 for 2,425/2,440.

The state-run Cotton Export Corporation said Pakistan's cotton output from the 1996/97 (July-June) crop had reached a provisional 8.735 million 375-lb bales by Thursday, down from 9.444 million in the same year-ago period.

The KCA said exporters had shipped 42,454 bales of cotton by April 23 compared to 1.77 million bales in the same time a year ago. Exporters had registered contracts for the export of 52,490 bales by April 29 compared to 2.32 million bales in the same time a year ago.
